# Diṭṭhikathā (Ps 1.2)

**ID:** Ps 1.2
**Section:** Paṭisambhidāmagga (ps)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Diṭṭhikathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0517m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Diṭṭhikathā* ("Discussion of Views") is the second treatise (Ps 1.2) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, located in the *Khuddaka Nikāya* [Frauwallner 1995; Wayman 1984]. Exemplifying the work's systematic and analytical method, the text opens with a catechismal interrogation: *kā diṭṭhi? kati diṭṭhiṭṭhānāni? kati diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānāni? kati diṭṭhiyo? kati diṭṭhābhinivesā? katamo diṭṭhiṭṭhānasamugghāto?* ("What is view? How many bases of views are there? How many obsessions of views? How many views? How many dogmatic adherences to views? What is the eradication of the basis of views?") [Frauwallner 1995]. It defines *diṭṭhi* as *abhinivesa-parāmāsa* ("holding on to conviction") and proceeds to illustrate how entities become objects of grasping, utilizing an extended list of nineteen faculties (*indriya*) alongside the aggregates (*khandha*), sense bases, and elements [Gethin 2001].

Doctrinally, the text classifies views into twenty modes of individuality or reifying view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*), applied in four ways across each of the five aggregates and designated as "aspects" (*ākāra*) [Wayman 1984]. The *Diṭṭhikathā* categorizes these into annihilationist views (*uccheda-diṭṭhi*)—such as observing any of the five aggregates as self—and eternalist views (*sassata-diṭṭhi*), such as observing the self as having form, form as being in self, or self as being in form [Wayman 1984].

- Mentioned in: SN 22.44 Paṭipadāsutta; Ds 2.3.1 Tikanikkhepa; Ne 20 Desanāhārasampāta; SA 69 其道; AN 4.200 Pemasutta; Vb 17 Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga; MN 109 (PTS MN iii 15) Mahāpuṇṇama Sutta; MN 44 (PTS MN i 299) Cūḷavedalla Sutta; SN 41.3 Dutiyaisidattasutta; Iti 49 (It 2.22 PTS It 43) Diṭṭhigata Sutta; Snp 1.7 (PTS Snp 21) Vasala Sutta

**Sources**

- [Frauwallner 1995] Erich Frauwallner, Studies in Abhidharma Literature and the Origins of Buddhist Philosophical Systems (1995) — Describes the opening catechismal questions of the Diṭṭhikathā.
- [Gethin 2001] Rupert M. Gethin, The Buddhist Path to Awakening: A Study of the Bodhi-Pakkhiyā Dhammā (2001 [1992]) — Explains the definition of diṭṭhi as abhinivesa-parāmāsa and the treatise's treatment of the extended faculties.
- [Wayman 1984] Alex Wayman, Buddhist Insight: Essays by Alex Wayman (1984) — Details the twenty aspects of identity view and their division into uccheda-diṭṭhi and sassata-diṭṭhi.
